title: Simple Baselines are Competitive with Code Evolution

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-based program search baselines evaluated on mathematical bounds, algorithm discovery, scaffold search, and MLE-Bench
mechanism.populationDetail: IID RS evaluates an independent temporary candidate batch, while SCS labels successive batches as generations; neither maintains an explicitly partitioned population.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The baselines select strong results for reporting, but do not describe a separate persistent elite archive.
mechanism.replacementDetail: SCS conditions each new batch on sampled runnable programs from the previous batch, but does not specify a survivor replacement rule or persistent population update.
mechanism.generationDetail: Both baselines generate complete programs from a task prompt; SCS conditions generation on prior runnable examples rather than asking the model to edit a selected parent.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: SCS reuses prior runnable programs and their task scores as conditioning examples; ordinary task metrics also rank candidates for final selection.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Neither IID RS nor SCS selects an editable parent. The previous-generation examples in SCS are reference context only; the paper explicitly distinguishes these baselines from fitness-based parent-selection evolutionary methods.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Sequential conditioning on uniformly sampled prior successful solutions without treating them as editable parents or maintaining a conventional survivor population.

provenance.citationWarning: The survey currently cites this paper under uniform single-parent selection, but the paper describes no editable parent selection. SCS uniformly samples three successful prior-generation programs as contextual references in its mathematical setup; recast the citation as reference-context selection or remove it from parent selection. Population/replacement labels are provisional because batches do not imply a maintained evolutionary population. Model configurations vary across distinct experiments and methods. Staged and repeated evaluation labels apply specifically to scaffold search.
